findings.category: A08 Software and Data Integrity / supply-chain
findings.title: Unverified third-party installer executed without checksum/signature
findings.description: tasks/main.yml lines 13-25 download https://install.ashwinchat.ai/ruflo via ansible.builtin.get_url with no `checksum:` parameter, then immediately bash-execute it. Trust relies solely on TLS to a third-party domain plus a self-reported `ruflo --version` string. If the upstream host is compromised (DNS hijack, CDN poisoning, domain expiry takeover, or a malicious release), the entire VM is compromised on the next `apply`. The `--version` post-check (line 34) only validates output text the installed binary chooses to print, so a backdoored binary can trivially fake the version match.
findings.impact: Full RCE on every target host on the next provision; pivots to Vaultwarden secrets (D24) and PK material referenced elsewhere in the stack. Affects every wave-3 deploy and every reprovision thereafter.
findings.recommendation: Either (a) pin a vendored installer copy in files/ and ship it from the role, or (b) add `checksum: sha256:<hex>` to the get_url task with a hash tied to ruflo_version. Additionally, verify the installed binary with a known-good hash (`stat` + `sha256sum` against a value pinned in defaults/main.yml) rather than relying on `ruflo --version` self-report. Consider GPG signature verification if upstream publishes signatures.

findings.title: validate_matrix.py has a runtime bug that makes the security control non-functional
findings.description: files/validate_matrix.py defines `validate_matrix()` returning a bare `int` on lines 132 and 135 (the success and error-aggregate paths), but only a `(int, str)` tuple on line 99 (config-dir-missing branch). Line 139 unconditionally unpacks: `exit_code, message = validate_matrix()`. Therefore on any normal run (config dir exists) the script raises `TypeError: cannot unpack non-iterable int object` before exiting, producing a non-zero exit purely from the bug — not from real validation. The task in tasks/main.yml:75 fails the role on rc!=0, so either (a) the role never converges in any environment where the matrix is correct (operationally broken), or (b) operators add `ignore_errors`/`failed_when: false` to work around the breakage, which kills the defense-in-depth control AC25–AC28 relies on. Either way the validator is effectively bypassed.
findings.impact: The matrix-correctness invariant (AC25–AC28 + tech-spec D17) is unenforced at runtime. A future drift — accidental edit, partial template render, attacker tampering — will not be detected by this script. The control exists on paper only.
findings.recommendation: Make `validate_matrix()` return a consistent type. Simplest fix: always return `int` and let the caller `sys.exit(validate_matrix())`. Add a molecule test that asserts `python validate_matrix.py; echo $?` is 0 on a healthy converge — this would have caught the bug. Also add a negative test that mutates one topic file and asserts the validator exits non-zero.

findings.title: Validator script lives in user-writable directory and can be replaced
findings.description: validate_matrix.py is copied to `~/.fabric/ruflo/validate_matrix.py` (mode 0750, owned by ansible_user). The same OS user that owns the ruflo runtime can rewrite the validator between Ansible runs to a no-op (`import sys; sys.exit(0)`). Because the role re-copies the script every run via `ansible.builtin.copy`, this is recovered on next apply — but in the window between applies (and especially in T18 where the validator is reused as a watchdog check), any process running as `ansible_user` can disable the check. There is no signature or hash pin of the script in the role.
findings.impact: An agent process — or a compromised topic engine running under the same UID — can locally suppress the matrix-correctness alarm. Defeats AC25–AC28 monitoring once T18 wires the validator into the watchdog.
findings.recommendation: Install the validator to `/usr/local/bin/ruflo-validate-matrix` owned by root, mode 0755; have ansible_user execute it via sudo with a NOPASSWD entry restricted to this exact command. Alternatively, compute a sha256 of the validator on copy and have the watchdog re-verify the hash before invoking it.

findings.title: no_log: true on installer hides both secrets and tampering evidence
findings.description: tasks/main.yml line 26 sets `no_log: true` on the installer shell task. The justification (installer may emit secrets) is reasonable, but combined with `changed_when: 'successfully' in ruflo_install_result.stdout | lower` (line 28) the controller has no record of installer output even on failure — including failure messages indicating MITM, version mismatch, or hostile output. There is no separate audit trail (file-based log) of the installer run.
findings.impact: Forensic blind spot. A supply-chain incident (finding 1) would leave no controller-side evidence beyond an opaque rc=0/rc!=0.
findings.recommendation: Either drop no_log (the installer is unlikely to print secrets — verify by inspection) or, if no_log is retained, redirect installer stdout/stderr to a root-owned 0600 log file on the target host (e.g. `/var/log/ruflo-install-{{ ansible_date_time.iso8601 }}.log`) so post-hoc forensic review is possible. Ensure the log path is excluded from the sanitizer's general scrub list (D26) since it is meant to be inspected.

findings.title: Installer artifact left in world-readable /tmp with predictable path
findings.description: tasks/main.yml downloads to `/tmp/ruflo-installer.sh` with mode 0755 (line 17) and never deletes it. Path is predictable and globally readable; any local unprivileged user can copy the installer (revealing its content and any embedded URLs/keys) or, if they win a race before mode-set, tamper with it. The bash execution (line 25) then runs whatever is on disk.
findings.impact: Local-user information disclosure of installer content; small but real TOCTOU window between download and execution if any other process can write to /tmp/ruflo-installer.sh.
findings.recommendation: Use `ansible.builtin.tempfile` to create a 0700 directory under root's home, download there with mode 0700, execute, then `ansible.builtin.file: state: absent` to clean up. Or pipe-execute the installer in-memory if upstream supports `curl | bash`-style invocation through a fetched-and-verified blob — but only after adding the checksum from finding 1.

findings.title: Templates don't validate rendered YAML
findings.description: Both global.yml.j2 and topics/topic.yml.j2 are written without `validate:` parameter on the template module. A future template typo could write syntactically invalid YAML that the validator only catches after the fact (and only if finding 2 is fixed).
findings.recommendation: Add `validate: 'python3 -c "import yaml,sys; yaml.safe_load(open(sys.argv[1]))" %s'` to both template tasks.

findings.title: Validator duplicates between handler and explicit task
findings.description: handlers/main.yml runs validate_matrix.py; tasks/main.yml lines 68-75 also run it explicitly afterwards. Functionally redundant. More importantly, the handler's failed_when would normally surface failures, but Ansible defers handler execution until the play ends — so failures in renders that should block further tasks won't, since validation runs last.
findings.impact: Minor design smell; the explicit task post-render does provide synchronous validation, so behavior is acceptable.
findings.recommendation: Drop the handler — the explicit post-render validation task is sufficient and synchronous.

findings.title: min_ansible_version 2.10 below current LTS
findings.description: meta/main.yml declares min_ansible_version 2.10. ansible-core 2.10 reached EOL years ago. While modules used here are stable across versions, declaring a supported floor below LTS implies the role is OK to run on unmaintained controllers.
findings.impact: Operators could deploy from an EOL controller missing recent security fixes.
findings.recommendation: Bump to ansible-core 2.15 or 2.16 (current LTS as of review date) to match the CI ansible-lint baseline.

findings.title: Validator uses `python` rather than `python3`
findings.description: tasks/main.yml:70 and handlers/main.yml:4 invoke `python ~/.fabric/ruflo/validate_matrix.py`. On Ubuntu 24.04 (per molecule platform image) `python` is not installed by default; only `python3` is. The molecule converge installs python3 explicitly, but the role itself does not. The validator's shebang is `#!/usr/bin/env python3` — call it directly rather than relying on an interpreter alias.
findings.impact: On a real target without the `python-is-python3` package, the validation step fails — and because of finding 2 the role already cannot converge on a healthy system; this compounds the operability problem and pressures operators to disable the check.
findings.recommendation: Either call `python3` explicitly, or execute the script directly (`cmd: '~/.fabric/ruflo/validate_matrix.py'` — it already has the shebang and 0750 mode).

positive_notes: Topic matrix in defaults/main.yml and CANONICAL_MATRIX in validate_matrix.py both match tech-spec §2.4 exactly across all 8 topics and all 7 fields.
MEMORY_NAMESPACE isolation per topic is correctly enforced: every topic gets a unique mnemonic-<topic> namespace; no namespace collision across topics.
aidefence-off on core and mcp is justified per user-spec AC27 (false positives on hex keys); not a finding.
rag_memory-off in protocol-qa is correctly enforced per AC26; protocol-qa is the only topic with that setting and the only one in mnemonic_mode=full, matching §2.4.
No hardcoded secrets, tokens, or credentials in any file under roles/ruflo/.
FQCN used consistently for every Ansible module (ansible.builtin.*); no bare module names.
Directory modes 0750 and file modes 0640 / 0750 for the validator are reasonable (group-readable but not world).
Idempotency contract is sound in principle: templates re-render from a single matrix variable; on-disk state is checked against canonical at the end.
no_log: true is correctly applied on the installer shell step (even though finding 4 critiques the trade-off, the principle is right).
Per-topic config files do not contain secrets — only toggles and namespace identifiers, so the 0640 mode is appropriate.
scope_observations: Reviewed: tasks/main.yml, defaults/main.yml, files/validate_matrix.py, templates/global.yml.j2, templates/topics/topic.yml.j2, handlers/main.yml, meta/main.yml, molecule/default/{converge,verify,molecule}.yml, README.md.
Cross-referenced: work/coding-fabric/tech-spec.md §2.3, §2.4, D17/D18; work/coding-fabric/user-spec.md AC25-AC28; work/coding-fabric/tasks/10.md acceptance criteria.
Findings 1, 4, 5 are blocking (changes_required). Findings 2 (validator unpacking bug) and 1 (no checksum) are the highest-leverage fixes — both are short and would close the most exploitable gaps.
Did not execute molecule or ansible-lint (read-only review). The reported ansible-lint clean status was not independently verified — recommend the next round confirm.

AC25–AC28 are anchored correctly on paper (matrix values match) but the runtime enforcement of those invariants is broken by finding 2; fixing the validator is required before AC25–AC28 can be considered met.
